title: Tax Crime and Money Laundering
summary: A six-module programme equipping tax, FIU and law-enforcement investigators to tackle tax crime and related laundering through information exchange and joint investigation.
intro: This training programme equips tax, FIU and law-enforcement investigators to tackle the overlap between tax crime and money laundering, from offshore structures and professional enablers to information exchange and joint investigations.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give tax investigators, FIU analysts and financial investigators a shared understanding of how tax crime and money laundering intersect, and how each agency's tools can strengthen the others' cases. Participants leave able to recognise the laundering of tax crime proceeds, use international information exchange, unpick offshore structures and run effective joint investigations.
sections.What It Covers: Tax crimes as predicate offences for money laundering, the OECD principles for fighting tax crime, offshore structures and beneficial ownership, exchange of information on request and automatically, inter-agency cooperation and joint investigations, professional enablers, and recovering the proceeds of tax crime.
Intended Audience: Tax crime investigators, tax auditors and revenue intelligence officers
FIU analysts and financial investigators handling tax-related intelligence
Prosecutors and asset recovery officers working on tax and laundering cases
Learning Objectives: Explain the links between tax crime and money laundering and the relevant international standards
Identify indicators of tax evasion and laundering in financial and tax data
Analyse offshore structures, nominee arrangements and beneficial ownership
Use exchange of information on request, automatically and spontaneously
Plan joint investigations across tax, FIU and law-enforcement agencies
Disrupt professional enablers and recover the proceeds of tax crime
sections.Structure and Format: Six modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a technical briefing with case studies and structure-mapping exercises, ending in a joint investigation workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the participating agencies.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of tax investigation, financial intelligence or financial crime work is helpful. No specialist knowledge of international tax law is required.
Core Reading: OECD (2021), Fighting Tax Crime – The Ten Global Principles, Second Edition
OECD (2019), Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Awareness Handbook for Tax Examiners and Tax Auditors
OECD (2021), Ending the Shell Game: Cracking down on the Professionals who enable Tax and White Collar Crimes
OECD (2017), Standard for Automatic Exchange of Financial Account Information in Tax Matters, Second Edition
FATF (2024), Guidance on Beneficial Ownership and Transparency of Legal Arrangements

modules.title: Tax Crime and Money Laundering: The Links
modules.summary: Why tax crimes are predicate offences for money laundering, how evasion and laundering overlap, and the international standards and principles that frame a joined-up response.
objectives: Explain tax crimes as predicate offences under the FATF standards
Distinguish evasion, avoidance and laundering of tax crime proceeds
Summarise the OECD Ten Global Principles for fighting tax crime
syllabus: Tax crimes as designated predicate offences
Evasion, aggressive avoidance and laundering compared
The OECD Ten Global Principles and national strategies
Common schemes: undeclared income, false invoicing and indirect tax fraud

modules.title: Offshore Structures, Secrecy and Beneficial Ownership
modules.summary: How companies, trusts, foundations and accounts in low-transparency jurisdictions are used to hide income and assets, and how investigators identify beneficial owners and controllers.
objectives: Recognise structures commonly used to conceal income and assets
Map ownership and control across several jurisdictions
Use beneficial ownership information while recognising its limits
syllabus: Offshore companies, trusts, foundations and nominee arrangements
Indicators of concealment and artificial arrangements
Beneficial ownership registers and service provider records
Mapping exercise: tracing a multi-layered structure

modules.title: International Exchange of Information
modules.summary: How tax authorities obtain information from abroad through exchange on request, automatic and spontaneous exchange, and how that information can, where permitted, support criminal investigations and FIU work.
objectives: Explain exchange on request, automatic exchange and spontaneous exchange
Use financial account and country-by-country data in investigations
Apply the conditions governing use of exchanged information for non-tax purposes
syllabus: Exchange on request and the standard of foreseeable relevance
The Common Reporting Standard and automatic exchange of financial account information
Spontaneous exchange and country-by-country reporting
Using tax information for non-tax purposes: conditions and gateways

modules.title: Inter-Agency Cooperation and Joint Investigations
modules.summary: Models of cooperation between tax administrations, FIUs, police and prosecutors, from information-sharing gateways to joint investigation teams, and how to make them work in practice.
objectives: Compare models of domestic inter-agency cooperation
Use the legal gateways between tax, FIU and law-enforcement agencies
Plan a joint investigation with clear governance and roles
syllabus: Models of cooperation: gateways, secondments and joint task forces
Tax access to FIU information and reporting of suspicions by tax officials
Joint investigation teams and international tax crime cooperation
Governance, confidentiality and case ownership

modules.title: Professional Enablers
modules.summary: How lawyers, accountants, tax advisers, trust and company service providers and financial professionals facilitate tax crime and laundering, and the tools available to investigate and disrupt them.
objectives: Identify the roles professional enablers play in tax and laundering schemes
Recognise indicators of complicit or negligent professional involvement
Apply criminal, civil, regulatory and disruptive responses to enablers
syllabus: Typologies of professional enablement
Legal professional privilege and access to professional records
Working with professional supervisors and self-regulatory bodies
Disruption strategies: prosecution, penalties and deterrence

modules.title: Recovering Proceeds and Joint Case Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining recovery of tax crime proceeds through criminal, civil and tax routes, ending with a workshop in which teams plan a joint tax and money laundering investigation.
objectives: Compare criminal confiscation, civil recovery and tax assessment as recovery routes
Coordinate recovery across tax and law-enforcement agencies
Apply the programme to plan a realistic joint investigation
syllabus: Tax assessments, penalties and criminal confiscation
Civil recovery and settlements in tax crime cases
Avoiding double recovery and coordinating enforcement
Workshop: the joint tax and laundering investigation plan

related.title: Asset Recovery: Tracing, Freezing and Confiscation
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping practitioners to trace, restrain, confiscate, manage and return criminal assets, including crypto-assets and assets held abroad.

related.title: Financial Investigation: Following the Money
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping investigators and analysts to run parallel financial investigations, trace funds through accounts and corporate vehicles, and present financial evidence.

related.title: FIU Operational and Strategic Analysis
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping FIU analysts to prioritise and analyse reports, produce operational and strategic intelligence, and cooperate effectively at home and abroad.

related.title: Fraud and Cyber-Enabled Financial Crime Investigations
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping investigators and FIU analysts to tackle fraud, money mules and ransomware proceeds, working with banks and payment firms to recover funds.

related.title: Prosecuting Financial Crime: Evidence, Experts and the Courtroom
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping prosecutors and judges to handle money laundering and complex financial crime cases, from charge and evidence to sentencing and confiscation.

related.title: Public-Private Partnerships and Financial Intelligence Sharing
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping FIUs and law-enforcement agencies to design, run and evaluate public-private partnerships for sharing financial intelligence lawfully and effectively.
